sanskrit: evaṃ bruvatyāṃ sītāyāṃ saṃrabdhaḥ paruṣākṣaram lalāṭe bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ pratyuvāca ha
english: As Sītā spoke thus, Rāvaṇa, enraged and harsh of speech, drew his brows together on his forehead and replied.

sanskrit: bhrātā vaiśravaṇasyāhaṃ sāpatnyo varavarṇini rāvaṇo nāma bhadraṃ te daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān
english: "I am the half-brother of Vaiśravaṇa, O fair-complexioned one — Rāvaṇa by name, be it known to you, the ten-necked one, mighty in valor."

sanskrit: yasya devāḥ sagandharvāḥ piśācapatagoragāḥ vidravanti bhayād bhītā mṛtyor iva sadā prajāḥ
english: "Before whom gods together with gandharvas, piśācas, birds, and serpents flee in terror, just as creatures flee always before Death."

sanskrit: yena vaiśravaṇo bhrātā vaimātraḥ kāraṇāntare dvandvam āsāditaḥ krodhād raṇe vikramya nirjitaḥ
english: "By whom Vaiśravaṇa, his half-brother, was on some occasion brought to single combat out of wrath, and was defeated in battle through valor."

sanskrit: madbhayārtaḥ parityajya svam adhiṣṭhānam ṛddhimat kailāsaṃ parvataśreṣṭham adhyāste naravāhanaḥ
english: "Tormented by fear of me, he abandoned his own prosperous abode and now dwells on Kailāsa, the best of mountains — he whose vehicle is men."

sanskrit: yasya tat puṣpakaṃ nāma vimānaṃ kāmagaṃ śubham vīryād āvarjitaḥ bhadre yena yāmi vihāyasaṃ
english: "Whose celestial chariot named Puṣpaka, lovely and going wherever one wills, was seized by force — O fair one — in which I travel through the sky."

sanskrit: mama saṃjātaroṣasya mukhaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva maithili vidravanti paritrastāḥ surāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ
english: "When my anger arises, the gods headed by Śakra flee in all directions, terrified, merely upon beholding my face, O Maithilī."

sanskrit: yatra tiṣṭhāmy ahaṃ tatra māruto vāti śaṅkitaḥ tīvrāṃśuḥ śiśirāṃśuś ca bhayāt saṃpadyate raviḥ
english: "Wherever I stand, the wind blows there with apprehension; the sun with his fierce rays becomes cool out of fear."

sanskrit: niṣkampapatrās taravo nadyaś ca stimitodakāḥ bhavanti yatra yatrāhaṃ tiṣṭhāmi ca carāmi ca
english: "Wherever I stand or move, the trees stand with their leaves motionless and the rivers with their waters stilled."

sanskrit: mama pāre samudrasya laṅkā nāma purī śubhā saṃpūrṇā rākṣasair ghorair yathendrasyāmarāvatī
english: "Beyond the ocean lies my beautiful city named Laṅkā, full of terrible rākṣasas, even as Amarāvatī is full of Indra's hosts."

sanskrit: prākāreṇa parikṣiptā pāṇḍureṇa virājitā hemakakṣyā purī ramyā vaidūryamaya toraṇā
english: "That lovely city is encircled by a gleaming white rampart, its inner courtyards of gold and its gateways of vaidūrya gems."

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathasaṃbhādhā tūryanādavināditā sarvakāmaphalair vṛkṣaiḥ saṃkulodyānaśobhitā
english: "Thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, resounding with the music of instruments, adorned with gardens teeming with trees that yield every desired fruit."

sanskrit: tatra tvaṃ vasatī sīte rājaputri mayā saha na sramiṣyasi nārīṇāṃ mānuṣīṇāṃ manasvini
english: "Living there with me, O Sītā, O princess, you will not tire of the pleasures of human women, O noble-minded one."

sanskrit: bhuñjānā mānuṣān bhogān divyāṃś ca varavarṇini na smariṣyasi rāmasya mānuṣasya gatāyuṣaḥ
english: "Enjoying both human and divine pleasures, O fair-complexioned one, you will not remember Rāma — a mere mortal whose life is spent."

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā priyaṃ putraṃ rājñā daśarathena yaḥ mandavīryaḥ suto jyeṣṭhas tataḥ prasthāpito vanam
english: "The eldest son, feeble in valor, who was sent to the forest by King Daśaratha after establishing his beloved other son on the throne —"

sanskrit: tena kiṃ bhraṣṭarājyena rāmeṇa gatacetasā kariṣyasi viśālākṣi tāpasena tapasvinā
english: "What will you do with that Rāma who has lost his kingdom, whose wits have gone astray, O wide-eyed one, that wretched ascetic of a hermit?"

sanskrit: sarvarākṣasabhartāraṃ kāmāt svayam ihāgatam na manmathaśarāviṣṭaṃ pratyākhyātuṃ tvam arhasi
english: "You ought not to reject me, the lord of all rākṣasas, who has come here of his own desire, who is pierced by the arrows of the love-god."

sanskrit: pratyākhyāya hi māṃ bhīru paritāpaṃ gamiṣyasi caraṇenābhihatyeva purūravasam urvaśī
english: "For having rejected me, O timid one, you will come to grief, as Urvaśī did when she struck away Purūravas with her foot."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī kruddhā saṃraktalocanā abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rahite rākṣasādhipam
english: Thus addressed, the daughter of Videha, angry and red-eyed, spoke harsh words to the lord of rākṣasas in that solitary place.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ devaṃ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam bhrātaraṃ vyapadiśya tvam aśubhaṃ kartum icchasi
english: "How do you desire to do evil, invoking as your own the divine Vaiśravaṇa, worshipped by all beings, as your brother?"

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ vinaśiṣyanti sarve rāvaṇa rākṣasāḥ yeṣāṃ tvaṃ karkaśo rājā durbuddhir ajitendriyaḥ
english: "All the rākṣasas will surely perish, O Rāvaṇa, whose king you are — harsh, evil-minded, with senses uncontrolled."

sanskrit: apahṛtya śacīṃ bhāryāṃ śakyam indrasya jīvitum na tu rāmasya bhāryāṃ mām apanīyāsti jīvitam
english: "One might carry off Śacī, Indra's wife, and still survive; but there is no life for anyone who carries me away, Rāma's wife."

sanskrit: jīvec ciraṃ vajradharasya hastāc chacīṃ pradhṛṣyāpratirūparūpām na mādṛśīṃ rākṣasadharṣayitvā pītāmṛtasyāpi tavāsti mokṣaḥ
english: "One might long survive having violated Śacī — of incomparable beauty — from the hand of the Vajra-bearer; but for one who has violated a woman like me, there is no escape, even if you have drunk the nectar of immortality."

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān haste hastaṃ samāhatya cakāra sumahad vapuḥ
english: Hearing Sītā's words, the mighty ten-necked one slapped one hand against the other and assumed a very great bodily form.

sanskrit: sa maithilīṃ punar vākyaṃ babhāṣe ca tato bhṛśam nonmattayā śrutau manye mama vīryaparākramau
english: He then spoke again insistently to the Maithilī: "I think you have not heard of my valor and might — you are surely mad."

sanskrit: udvaheyaṃ bhujābhyāṃ tu medinīm ambare sthitaḥ āpibeyaṃ samudraṃ ca mṛtyuṃ hanyāṃ raṇe sthitaḥ
english: "Standing in the sky, I could lift the earth with these arms; I could drink the ocean dry, and standing in battle I could slay Death himself."

sanskrit: arkaṃ rundhyāṃ śarais tīkṣṇair vibhindyāṃ hi mahītalam kāmarūpiṇam unmatte paśya māṃ kāmadaṃ patim
english: "I could block out the sun with sharp arrows; I could split the very earth asunder. O madwoman, see me, who take whatever form I will — I am a husband who grants every desire."

sanskrit: evam uktavatas tasya rāvaṇasya śikhiprabhe kruddhasya hariparyante rakte netre babhūvatuḥ
english: As Rāvaṇa thus spoke, his two eyes — edged with yellow, blazing like fire — became red with rage.

sanskrit: sadyaḥ saumyaṃ parityajya bhikṣurūpaṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ svaṃ rūpaṃ kālarūpābhaṃ bheje vaiśravaṇānujaḥ
english: Instantly casting off the gentle form of a mendicant, Rāvaṇa — the younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa — assumed his own form, resembling the form of Death.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayanaḥ śrīmāṃs taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ daśāsyaḥ kārmukī bāṇī babhūva kṣaṇadācaraḥ
english: With blood-red eyes, resplendent, wearing earrings of molten gold, ten-faced, bearing bow and arrows — thus did the ranger of the night appear.

sanskrit: sa parivrājakacchadma mahākāyo vihāya tat pratipede svakaṃ rūpaṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Abandoning the disguise of a wandering mendicant, that great-bodied Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, resumed his own true form.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayanaḥ krodhāj jīmūtanicayaprabhaḥ raktāmbaradharas tasthau strīratnaṃ prekṣya maithilīm
english: With eyes reddened by anger, blazing like a mass of storm-clouds, clad in crimson garments, he stood gazing upon the Maithilī, that jewel among women.

sanskrit: sa tām asitakeśāntāṃ bhāskarasya prabhām iva vasanābharaṇopetāṃ maithilīṃ rāvaṇo 'bravīt
english: Then Rāvaṇa spoke to that Maithilī, whose hair-ends were dark, who shone like the sun's radiance, adorned with garments and ornaments.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ yadi bhartāram icchasi mām āśraya varārohe tavāhaṃ sadṛśaḥ patiḥ
english: "If you desire a husband renowned in the three worlds, take refuge in me, O fair-hipped one — I am a fitting husband for you."

sanskrit: māṃ bhajasva cirāya tvam ahaṃ ślāghyas tava priyaḥ naiva cāhaṃ kva cid bhadre kariṣye tava vipriyam tyajyatāṃ mānuṣo bhāvo mayi bhāvaḥ praṇīyatām
english: "Give yourself to me for all time — I am worthy of praise, I shall be your beloved; O fair one, never shall I do you any displeasure. Abandon your attachment to a mortal; direct your heart toward me."

sanskrit: rājyāc cyutam asiddhārthaṃ rāmaṃ parimitāyuṣam kair guṇair anuraktāsi mūḍhe paṇḍitamānini
english: "What virtues could make you attached to Rāma — fallen from his kingdom, his purpose unaccomplished, of limited lifespan — you fool, who consider yourself wise?"

sanskrit: yaḥ striyā vacanād rājyaṃ vihāya sasuhṛjjanam asmin vyālānucarite vane vasati durmatiḥ
english: "That one of evil mind who, at a woman's word, abandoned his kingdom and his companions and now lives in this forest haunted by serpents —"

sanskrit: ity uktvā maithilīṃ vākyaṃ priyārhāṃ priyavādinīm jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ budhaḥ khe rohiṇīm iva
english: Having spoken thus to the Maithilī — who deserved only kind treatment, who spoke sweet words — Rāvaṇa seized Sītā as the planet Mercury seizes Rohiṇī in the sky.

sanskrit: vāmena sītāṃ padmākṣīṃ mūrdhajeṣu kareṇa saḥ ūrvos tu dakṣiṇenaiva parijagrāha pāṇinā
english: With his left hand he grasped lotus-eyed Sītā by her hair, and with his right hand he clasped her about the thighs.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgābhaṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ mahābhujam prādravan mṛtyusaṃkāśaṃ bhayārtā vanadevatāḥ
english: Beholding him — towering like a mountain peak, sharp-fanged, long-armed, resembling Death — the forest deities fled away in terror.

sanskrit: sa ca māyāmayo divyaḥ kharayuktaḥ kharasvanaḥ pratyadṛśyata hemāṅgo rāvaṇasya mahārathaḥ
english: And there appeared Rāvaṇa's great chariot — wrought of illusion, divine, yoked with braying asses, its body of gold, resounding with a harsh din.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ paruṣair vākyair abhitarjya mahāsvanaḥ aṅkenādāya vaidehīṃ ratham āropayat tadā
english: Then that great-voiced one, having terrified her with harsh words, lifted the daughter of Videha into his lap and placed her upon the chariot.

sanskrit: sā gṛhītāticukrośa rāvaṇena yaśasvinī rāmeti sītā duḥkhārtā rāmaṃ dūragataṃ vane
english: Seized thus, the glorious Sītā cried out with a great shriek in her distress: "Rāma!" — to Rāma who was far away in the forest.

sanskrit: tām akāmāṃ sa kāmārtaḥ pannagendravadhūm iva viveṣṭamānām ādāya utpapāthātha rāvaṇaḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa, consumed by desire, lifted her who was unwilling — struggling and twisting like the wife of the king of serpents — and soared upward.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā rākṣasendreṇa hriyamāṇā vihāyasā bhṛśaṃ cukrośa matteva bhrāntacittā yathāturā
english: Then she, being carried away through the sky by the lord of rākṣasas, cried out loudly, like one maddened, her mind bewildered, as though stricken by illness.

sanskrit: hā lakṣmaṇa mahābāho gurucittaprasādaka hriyamāṇāṃ na jānīṣe rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā
english: "O Lakṣmaṇa, O great-armed one, who bring joy to the heart of your elder — you do not know that I am being carried away by a rākṣasa who takes any form he wills!"

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ sukham arthāṃś ca dharmahetoḥ parityajan hriyamāṇām adharmeṇa māṃ rāghava na paśyasi
english: "O Rāghava, you who have abandoned life, happiness, and wealth for the sake of righteousness — do you not see me being carried away in unrighteousness?"

sanskrit: nanu nāmāvinītānāṃ vinetāsi paraṃtapa katham evaṃvidhaṃ pāpaṃ na tvaṃ śādhi hi rāvaṇam
english: "Are you not the subduer of the arrogant, O scorcher of foes? How is it you do not chastise Rāvaṇa for this wicked deed?"

sanskrit: nanu sadyo 'vinītasya dṛśyate karmaṇaḥ phalam kālo 'py aṅgī bhavaty atra sasyānām iva paktaye
english: "Surely the fruit of an arrogant man's deed is seen quickly; even Time here becomes a participant, as in the ripening of a harvest."

sanskrit: sa karma kṛtavān etat kālopahatacetanaḥ jīvitāntakaraṃ ghoraṃ rāmād vyasanam āpnuhi
english: "He has committed this deed with a mind struck by doom — he will suffer from Rāma a terrible calamity that brings his life to an end."

sanskrit: hantedānīṃ sakāmā tu kaikeyī bāndhavaiḥ saha hriyeyaṃ dharmakāmasya dharmapatnī yaśasvinaḥ
english: "Alas, now Kaikeyī together with her kinsmen will be gratified, for I — the lawful and glorious wife of the righteous and desiring-of-virtue Rāma — am being carried away."

sanskrit: āmantraye janasthānaṃ karṇikārāṃś ca puṣpitān kṣipraṃ rāmāya śaṃsadhvaṃ sītāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "I take my leave of Janasthāna and of the blooming karṇikāra trees — quickly announce to Rāma: Rāvaṇa is carrying Sītā away!"

sanskrit: mālyavantaṃ śikhariṇaṃ vande prasravaṇaṃ girim kṣipraṃ rāmāya śaṃsadhvaṃ sītāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "I salute Mālyavān, Śikharī, and the mountain Prasravaṇa — quickly announce to Rāma: Rāvaṇa is carrying Sītā away!"

sanskrit: haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭāṃ vande godāvarīṃ nadīm kṣipraṃ rāmāya śaṃsadhvaṃ sītāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "I salute the Godāvarī river resounding with swans and sārasa cranes — quickly announce to Rāma: Rāvaṇa is carrying Sītā away!"

sanskrit: daivatāni ca yānty asmin vane vividhapādape namaskaromy ahaṃ tebhyo bhartuḥ śaṃsata māṃ hṛtām
english: "And the divinities that reside in the various trees of this forest — I bow to them all: announce to my husband that I have been abducted."

sanskrit: yāni kāni cid apy atra sattvāni nivasanty uta sarvāṇi śaraṇaṃ yāmi mṛgapakṣigaṇān api
english: "Whatever beings live here as well — I take refuge in all of them, even in the herds of deer and the flocks of birds."

sanskrit: hriyamāṇāṃ priyāṃ bhartuḥ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm vivaśāpahṛtā sītā rāvaṇeneti śaṃsata
english: "Tell him: 'Sītā, dearer to her husband than life itself, has been carried away helpless by Rāvaṇa — she has been abducted.'"

sanskrit: viditvā māṃ mahābāhur amutrāpi mahābalaḥ āneṣyati parākramya vaivasvatahṛtām api
english: "Knowing of me, the great-armed and mighty one will retrieve me by his valor even from the beyond — even from one taken by Vaivasvata himself."

sanskrit: rāmāya tu yathātattvaṃ jaṭāyo haraṇaṃ mama lakṣmaṇāya ca tat sarvam ākhyātavyam aśeṣataḥ
english: "O Jaṭāyu, you must faithfully report the whole account of my abduction to Rāma and to Lakṣmaṇa, completely and without remainder."

sanskrit: taṃ śabdam avasuptasya jaṭāyur atha śuśruve niraikṣad rāvaṇaṃ kṣipraṃ vaidehīṃ ca dadarśa saḥ
english: Jaṭāyu, who had been asleep, heard that cry and quickly beheld Rāvaṇa and saw the daughter of Videha.

sanskrit: tataḥ parvatakūṭābhas tīkṣṇatuṇḍaḥ khagottamaḥ vanaspatigataḥ śrīmān vyājahāra śubhāṃ giram
english: Then that best of birds, resplendent as a mountain peak, with a sharp beak, perched upon a forest tree, uttered a clear and noble speech.

sanskrit: daśagrīvasthito dharme purāṇe satyasaṃśrayaḥ jaṭāyur nāma nāmnāhaṃ gṛdhrarājo mahābalaḥ
english: "O ten-necked one, I stand in ancient dharma, grounded in truth — I am named Jaṭāyu, king of vultures, and I am mighty."

sanskrit: rājā sarvasya lokasya mahendravaruṇopamaḥ lokānāṃ ca hite yukto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
english: "Rāma, son of Daśaratha, comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa, is king of all the worlds and is devoted to the welfare of those worlds."

sanskrit: tasyaiṣā lokanāthasya dharmapatnī yaśasvinī sītā nāma varārohā yāṃ tvaṃ hartum ihecchasi
english: "This glorious and fair-hipped woman named Sītā, the lawful wife of that lord of the world — it is she whom you desire to carry off."

sanskrit: kathaṃ rājā sthito dharme paradārān parāmṛśet rakṣaṇīyā viśeṣeṇa rājadārā mahābalaḥ nivartaya matiṃ nīcāṃ paradārābhimarśanam
english: "How could a king who abides in dharma lay hands upon another's wife? The wife of a king must especially be protected, O great one. Turn back your base intent of violating another's wife."

sanskrit: na tat samācared dhīro yat paro 'sya vigarhayet yathātmanas tathānyeṣāṃ dārā rakṣyā vimarśanāt
english: "A wise man should not do what others would condemn in him; upon reflection, the wives of others must be protected as one's own."

sanskrit: arthaṃ vā yadi vā kāmaṃ śiṣṭāḥ śāstreṣv anāgatam vyavasyanty anu rājānaṃ dharmaṃ paurastyanandana
english: "The learned, in matters of artha or kāma not explicitly covered in the śāstras, determine dharma by following the example of the king, O delight of the eastern people."

sanskrit: rājā dharmaś ca kāmaś ca dravyāṇāṃ cottamo nidhiḥ dharmaḥ śubhaṃ vā pāpaṃ vā rājamūlaṃ pravartate
english: "The king is dharma, and kāma, and the supreme treasury of wealth; whether dharma issues in good or evil — it proceeds with the king as its root."

sanskrit: pāpasvabhāvaś capalaḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ rakṣasāṃ vara aiśvaryam abhisaṃprāpto vimānam iva duṣkṛtī
english: "Evil by nature and fickle — how have you, O best of rākṣasas, come to possess sovereignty, like a sinner who has somehow boarded a celestial chariot?"

sanskrit: kāmasvabhāvo yo yasya na sa śakyaḥ pramārjitum na hi duṣṭātmanām ārya mā vasaty ālaye ciram
english: "A man's inherent nature cannot be wiped away; O noble one — nay, do not pursue this — prosperity does not dwell long in the house of those with corrupt souls."

sanskrit: viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā rāmo mahābalaḥ nāparādhyati dharmātmā kathaṃ tasyāparādhyasi
english: "When the mighty Rāma, righteous of soul, has committed no offense against your realm or city, how do you transgress against him?"

sanskrit: yadi śūrpaṇakhāhetor janasthānagataḥ kharaḥ ativṛtto hataḥ pūrvaṃ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: "If Khara, stationed at Janasthāna, transgressed and was formerly slain by Rāma of effortless action — that was on account of Śūrpaṇakhā's instigation."

sanskrit: atra brūhi yathāsatyaṃ ko rāmasya vyatikramaḥ yasya tvaṃ lokanāthasya hṛtvā bhāryāṃ gamiṣyasi
english: "Tell the truth here: what transgression of Rāma's is it — on account of which you would carry off the wife of that lord of the world?"

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ visṛja vaidehīṃ mā tvā ghoreṇa cakṣuṣā dahed dahana bhūtena vṛtram indrāśanir yathā
english: "Release the daughter of Videha at once, lest his terrible gaze burn you — blazing like fire — as Indra's thunderbolt burned Vṛtra."

sanskrit: sarpam āśīviṣaṃ baddhvā vastrānte nāvabudhyase grīvāyāṃ pratimuktaṃ ca kālapāśaṃ na paśyasi
english: "Binding a venomous serpent in the hem of your garment, you do not perceive it; nor do you see the noose of Death fastened about your neck."

sanskrit: sa bhāraḥ saumya bhartavyo yo naraṃ nāvasādayet tad annam upabhoktavyaṃ jīryate yad anāmayam
english: "That burden alone is worth bearing, O gentle one, which does not weigh a man down; that food alone is worth eating which, when digested, causes no illness."

sanskrit: yat kṛtvā na bhaved dharmo na kīrtir na yaśo bhuvi śarīrasya bhavet khedaḥ kas tat karma samācaret
english: "An act that produces no dharma, no fame, no glory in this world, but only distress for the body — who would undertake such a deed?"

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi mama jātasya rāvaṇa pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ yathāvad anutiṣṭhataḥ
english: "For sixty thousand years since my birth, O Rāvaṇa, have I been duly following the ancestral and grandfatherly path of kingship."

sanskrit: vṛddho 'haṃ tvaṃ yuvā dhanvī sarathaḥ kavacī śarī tathāpy ādāya vaidehīṃ kuśalī na gamiṣyasi
english: "Old as I am, and young as you are — an archer mounted on a chariot, armored and bearing arrows — even so you will not depart safely with the daughter of Videha."

sanskrit: na śaktas tvaṃ balād dhartuṃ vaidehīṃ mama paśyataḥ hetubhir nyāyasaṃyuktair dhruvāṃ vedaśrutīm iva
english: "You are not capable of forcibly carrying away the daughter of Videha before my eyes — no more than one can remove a firmly grounded Vedic truth by means of clever arguments."

sanskrit: yudhyasva yadi śūro 'si muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha rāvaṇa śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathāpūrvaṃ kharas tathā
english: "Fight if you are a hero — stand your ground a moment, Rāvaṇa — you will lie slain upon the earth, just as Khara did before."

sanskrit: asakṛt saṃyuge yena nihatā daityadānavāḥ nacirāc cīravāsās tvāṃ rāmo yudhi vadhiṣyati
english: "By whom daityas and dānavas have been slain again and again in battle — that bark-clad Rāma will slay you in combat before long."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ gatau dūraṃ nṛpātmajau kṣipraṃ tvaṃ naśyase nīca tayor bhīto na saṃśayaḥ
english: "What can I do, when those two princes are gone so far away? You surely flee quickly, O base one — you are without doubt afraid of them."

sanskrit: na hi me jīvamānasya nayiṣyasi śubhām imām sītāṃ kamalapatrākṣīṃ rāmasya mahaṣīṃ priyām
english: "While I yet live, you shall not carry away this beautiful one — lotus-eyed Sītā, the beloved great wife of Rāma."

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā kāryaṃ priyaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ jīvitenāpi rāmasya tathā daśarathasya ca
english: "I must assuredly do what is dear to that great-souled Rāma — even at the cost of my life — and likewise what is dear to Daśaratha."

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha daśagrīva muhūrtaṃ paśya rāvaṇa yuddhātithyaṃ pradāsyāmi yathāprāṇaṃ niśācara vṛntād iva phalaṃ tvāṃ tu pātayeyaṃ rathottamāt
english: "Stop, stop, O ten-necked one — wait a moment, behold, Rāvaṇa — I shall offer you the hospitality of battle to the full measure of my life, O ranger of the night; I shall bring you down from your magnificent chariot like a fruit from its stalk."
